To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a TeV scale neutrino mass texture that leads to a large mixing between the light and the heavy neutrinos, can be realized in the framework of quark lepton unifications; (ii) the model is strongly constrained, in particular by the lepton universality violating process µ → e, which requires the mixing between the light neutrinos and the heavy neutrino to be large.

the Z-pole and NuTeV data are consistent with the seesaw mechanism if the neutrinos are mixed with heavy gauge singlets and if the mass texture is such that the mixing angle is large and lepton flavor violation in the charged channel occurs.

the Z-pole measurements from the LEP and SLC colliders and the NuTeV experiment are in conflict with each other and the conflict is resolved by introducing heavy gauge singlet neutrinos that mix with the light neutrinos.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neutrino sector of the Standard Model has been extended by a few TeV scale gauge singlets, and that the lepton flavor non-conservation is not only allowed but also required.
the neutrino mass matrix is not diagonal in the basis where the charged lepton mass matrix is diagonal.

the seesaw mechanism can explain the data if the heavy gauge singlet fermions are in the few TeVs range, and that the lepton flavor non-conservation is a necessary consequence of the seesaw mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the seesaw mechanism can naturally be extended to the TeV scale and that the lepton flavor non-conserving processes are a natural consequence of this mechanism.
the neutrino mass matrix is a 3 × 3 matrix, and it has a texture of the form M = M 1 + M 2.

we are able to explain the NuTeV anomaly by introducing a new heavy gauge singlet state, while keeping the lepton flavor nonuniversality in the charged channel within the reach of the present and near-future experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a TeV scale neutrino mass mechanism can be consistent with both the Z-pole and NuTeV data.
the seesaw mechanism can be made to work with the heavy states being within the reach of the Large Hadron Collider.
the seesaw mechanism may be operative at the TeV scale and that it may be possible to probe its effects at a TeV scale collider.
